text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.26% today, continuing a sharp downward slide that began on November 18th—the stock dropped roughly $5.70 (4%) in just two trading days. That sell-off coincides with oil prices sliding notably lower: US crude fell to $89.53 per barrel today from around $98–$100 just days prior. Since oil companies' profits depend directly on the prices they can sell oil for, a drop of this magnitude hits their valuations hard, even if it reflects broader energy market weakness rather than problems specific to the company.

The Middle East tension you might expect to support oil prices—Iran attacking US military installations in the Gulf, threats to the Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor—hasn't prevented the decline, suggesting that other factors (global growth concerns, shifts in energy demand expectations, or rotation out of energy stocks) are overriding geopolitical risk premiums for now.
